7	### THE CENTRAL STORY: Ostrey Hollow milk-testing station and the Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association
8	
9	#### Geography / entities
10	- **Larrow Valley** — the valley; contains **Larrow Green** (site of the main creamery, on Larrow Creek, built 1891) and, seven miles up-valley, **Ostrey Hollow**, at the head of which stood the **skimming station**.
11	- **Hessel Bottom** — a wet meadow below the Ostrey Hollow hamlet; the best milk in the Hollow came from here. Seven farms had grazing/haying rights on Hessel Bottom (per r02/Effie Loomis) — but Roy Brant (r09) says **six farms**; the largest was **Emmet Brant's** (per r02) — confirmed independently by Roy Brant (r09): the Brant farm was "the largest of the six — sixty-odd acres of the meadow, and thirty-eight cows in a good year." "Six farms" is now corroborated by FIVE independent sources (r09, r15/Grigg's 1908 committee report, r16/Kepp, r17/Hazel Brant, plus the underlying 1908 report itself) against r02/Loomis's lone "seven."
12	- **Ashlin** — the county seat/town where hearings, the Association's office (later), the historical society, and legal business took place. Per r17: the Brant weigh book was held "down the street at the historical rooms in this town" of Ashlin — "where anybody may look at it who wants to, which is nobody." Per r18/Duncan Keddie: confirmed and expanded — the Brant weigh book went to the "Ordell County Historical Rooms" in Ashlin in 1963 (given by Hazel Brant); the station test book also went there in 1959. "Ordell County" is now given as the formal county name (previously only "Ordell County Bar Association," "Ordell County Farm Club," "Ordell dairy-inspection circuit" had appeared — now explicitly the county containing Ashlin and the Historical Rooms).
13	- **Farland** — site of a college with a library (where Ivy Keddie later worked/taught/studied, and where Merle Strawn's notebooks were held). The State Agricultural College at Farland published Bulletin No. 214 (1911, feeding trial on bog hay) and Bulletin No. 471 (1958, final exoneration).
14	- **Redlow Ridge**, **Vessey County** — location of the **Alder Corners Cheese Company** (a rival/comparison creamery, used for cross-checking milk tests). Per r10 (Rosalie Cudd): the ridge is a 4-mile switchback road, cut for a lumber road, shuts in November and does not open before April (some years May); "no arguing with it."
15	- **Tarnet** — per r17/Hazel Brant, the place the pipette crate "came out from... in ninety-nine" (1899) — a supplier/origin location and date for the crate, in tension with the established 1897 Ammon & Sons invoice date (see conflicts below).
16	- **Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association** — organized 1889 by valley farmers at Larrow Green. By-laws drafted by **Gideon Vose**, who was elected first president in 1889 and served until 1911 (22 years — longest of any president). Gideon Vose died in 1917.
